title: Microsoft Purview: OCR scanning of images for DLP in SharePoint and OneDrive (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, general OCR controls and metered licensing are supported, and it distinguishes government-cloud plans from current documentation. Minor corrections should complete the control paths and acknowledge differences between Microsoft pages about image limits, TIFF billing and insider risk preview status.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans Purview OCR to detect sensitive content in images and apply DLP policies in SharePoint Online and OneDrive.
claims.quote: Optical character recognition (OCR) support will detect sensitive content in images and subsequently apply data loss prevention (DLP) policies to prevent exfiltration of that sensitive data in SharePoint Online and OneDrive.

claims.claim: The roadmap names JPG, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, BMP and image-only PDF.
claims.quote: This release supports key file types like JPG, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, BMP, and PDF (image-only PDF).

claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Microsoft's Zero Trust guidance says DLP and auto-labeling cannot scan image-based content without OCR.
claims.quote: Without OCR, DLP policies, and auto-labeling policies can't scan image-based content, scanned documents, screenshots, and invoices, leaving sensitive data in images unprotected.

claims.claim: Backfill is restricted to OCR-enabled sites.
claims.quote: OCR backfill can only be run on OCR-enabled sites.

claims.claim: The backfill reference does not state government-cloud applicability.

claims.quote: When you apply OCR to a PDF or TIFF file, the extracted text is indexed in search but not available in the metadata column.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Each PDF page is charged separately, so a ten-page PDF counts as ten scans.
claims.quote: Each page in a PDF file is charged separately. For example, if there are 10 pages in a PDF file, an OCR scan of the PDF file counts as 10 separate scans.
